title: Increasing and Decreasing
description: Shape crochet fabric by adding or removing stitches without losing count.

content.summary: Learn how to make two stitches in one space to increase, and combine stitches to decrease.
content.whyItMatters: Shaping lets you build flat circles, rounded forms, and neater fitted pieces instead of only flat rectangles.
steps: To increase, work two stitches into the same stitch or space.
To decrease in single crochet, insert into the next stitch, pull up a loop, insert into the following stitch, pull up a loop, then yarn over and pull through all loops.
Count stitches at the end of each row or round so shaping stays intentional.
Practice placing increases evenly so the fabric stays flat instead of ruffling.
content.practice: Make one swatch with paired increases and one swatch with simple decreases, then count the stitches after each row.
commonMistakes: Increasing in random places and accidentally warping the fabric.
Forgetting where the decrease started and dropping a stitch from the count.
